title: Run Ticker Notebook - personal mini-sheet
content:
TABLE: quick run ticks (personal)

Columns: RunID | Variant | Batch | Quant | Tokens | p95_ms | avg_ms | cost_per_1k_usd | quality_score | notes
R-101 | rwd-v1-7b | 1 | fp16 | 512 | 86 | 42 | 0.012 | 0.82 | baseline single-shot, trunc@512
R-102 | rwd-v1-7b-q8 | 4 | int8 | 512 | 120 | 67 | 0.009 | 0.79 | batching ↑ throughput, p95 tail worse on mixed seqs
R-103 | llama-like-13b | 1 | fp16 | 1024 | 210 | 115 | 0.035 | 0.88 | quality nice, cost high; note: CPU spikes during kv cache load
R-104 | rwd-v1-7b-kvcache | 8 | int8 | 256 | 95 | 38 | 0.007 | 0.80 | warm-cache wins on repeated prefixes; warm-up penalty ~30ms
R-105 | rwd-v1-13b-q4 | 2 | q4_0 | 768 | 170 | 98 | 0.015 | 0.81 | hallucination rate seemed higher on factual prompts
R-106 | fallback-gptx-lite | 1 | fp16 | 256 | 50 | 28 | 0.045 | 0.75 | super low tail, cost-per-token spike due to licensing overhead

QUICK TAKEAWAYS (me):
- Small batches (1-2) keep avg latency low; batching (4-8) helps throughput but increases p95 on hetero lengths.
- Quant/int8 gives cost wins but watch p95 on long-history prompts.
- KV-cache is worth it for repeat-session flows; measure warm-up on cold-start window.
- Quality tradeoffs: 13b class -> better scores but >2x cost for many workloads.

NOTES TO SELF (rough):

- add p99 column next pass, want tail story (esp when batching mixed seqs).
- re-run R-102 with controlled seq-length bucket (256/512/1024) to isolate tail cause.
- check infra: why CPU spikes on R-103? link to PR-1824 (runtime memory change) — ask @Zara
